newsitem.title: FRANCE: French war correspondent Yves Heller dies at 50.
newsitem.headline: French war correspondent Yves Heller dies at 50.

text.p: Yves Heller, one of France's most respected war correspondents, who covered conflicts across the Middle East and Africa for the newspaper Le Monde and Agence France-Presse, has died aged 50, Le Monde said on Friday.
Heller, described by Le Monde as a "prince among roving reporters", died of heart failure on Thursday in Paris.

On assignments with the French news agency, the fearless reporter covered the 1979 Iranian revolution and hostage crisis, the 1982 Israeli invasion of Lebanon and fighting in Afghanistan, Chad and Ethiopia.

After joining Le Monde in 1987, he helped cover the Palestinian uprising and the Balkans, where he was among the first journalists to forecast the bloody breakup of former Yugoslavia and report on ethnic cleansing.
Most recently, he was deputy features editor.

Le Monde foreign editor Alain Frachon praised Heller as an even-handed reporter of great integrity and modesty. He quoted a Lebanese colleague as saying: "Yves was always courteous and warm-hearted with us in the air raid shelters, because he knew that we were condemned to stay here when he went back to Paris."
He leaves a wife and two children.
